newsitem.title: POLAND: Pope urges "end to the plague of hunger".
newsitem.headline: Pope urges "end to the plague of hunger".

text.p: Pope John Paul, saying thousands of deaths each year from starvation weighed on the world's conscience, urged an international campaign on Sunday "to put an end to the plague of hunger."
The pontiff told the first open air mass of his latest pilgrimage to his homeland:

"In an era of unprecedented technical development and new technology, the trauma of hunger is a great challenge and indictment. The earth can feed everybody. Why then today are thousands of people dying of hunger?"

His message was delivered after a religious congress in the southern city of Wroclaw attended by Church leaders of all denominations from across the world, including Africa and Asia where food shortages are worst.

The plight of the starving has been a Vatican priority especially since a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit in Rome last November which pledged to halve the world's population of 840 million starving people by 2015.
The U.N. Food and Agricultural Organisation (FAO) estimates that food production must rise 75 percent over the next 30 years to meet the needs of the world's growing population.
The Pope aimed his appeal at political and business leaders "on whom lies the responsibility for a just sharing of resources on a world scale."

He added: "We must at last put an end to the plague of hunger. Let solidarity take precedence over unbridled lust for profit and the application of those market principles which do not take account of inalienable human rights."
Although the United States, the world's biggest food provider, and other wealthy countries signed the Rome summit texts, they rejected the concept that access to food was a "human right".
Washington believes free trade is the key to ending poverty and hunger and fears that recognising a "right to food" could lead to law suits from poor nations seeking aid and trade privileges.
The United States did not agree to the food summit target for each country to spend 0.7 percent of annual economic wealth on development aid.
